mainTopic: The size of a סנהדרין קטנה and the judges in the desert, the end of פרק דיני ממונות, and the opening משנה and גמרא on the laws of the כהן גדול and the king
overview: The amud opens by finishing a calculation: a city needs 277 people to have its own סנהדרין קטנה. A ברייתא in the name of רבי says 278. The גמרא answers that the numbers depend on whether the סנהדרין גדולה has 70 judges (רבי יהודה) or 71 (רבנן). A ברייתא then counts the judges appointed in the desert and reaches 78,600. After the הדרן closing פרק דיני ממונות, a new פרק opens with a משנה about the כהן גדול. It covers court, testimony, חליצה, יבום, funerals and mourning. It then contrasts him with the king, who takes no part in any of these and whose widow may not remarry, though רבי יהודה disagrees on some points. The גמרא asks why the משנה needs to say that a כהן גדול judges and is judged. It gives two answers: the line is there to stand beside the king's rule, or it teaches that the כהן גדול is like an ordinary person before the law. Examining that ברייתא, the גמרא explains why a כהן גדול who kills by accident must still go into exile, and it begins quoting a משנה that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The final number: 277 people
steps.stepSummary: The calculation from the previous lines ends: a city needs 277 people to be fit for a סנהדרין קטנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Two hundred and seventy-seven.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the calculation it began earlier and gives the final count: 277 people in a city.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This follows the approach of רבי נחמיה that was built up earlier: 230 people as the base, plus 47 extra. The 47 are there in case the 23 judges cannot reach a decision and more judges are added, all the way up to 70.
steps.confusionAlert: This number is not a new statement. It is the end of a calculation that started before this section.

phrases.english: Two hundred and seventy-seven.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the population calculation begun before this section.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A city needs 277 people to be fit for a סנהדרין קטנה.

steps.title: A ברייתא that says 278
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the number 277 with a ברייתא in which רבי says 278.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was taught in a ברייתא: רבי says, two hundred and seventy-eight!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points to another ברייתא that gives a different number, 278, and asks how this fits with 277.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both numbers are said in the name of רבי, so they seem to contradict each other. The difference is only one person, and the גמרא wants to know where that one extra person comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: But it was taught in a ברייתא (introduces a challenge)
רבי יהודה הנשיא, who compiled the משנה

phrases.english: But it was taught: רבי says:
Two hundred and seventy-eight!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the number 277 given in step 1.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא in רבי's name gives 278, which contradicts 277.

steps.title: It depends on 70 or 71 judges
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that 277 follows רבי יהודה and 278 follows רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult: this one follows רבי יהודה, and that one follows the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction by saying each number follows a different opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה holds that the סנהדרין גדולה has 70 judges, so the court can grow by 47 (23 + 47 = 70), which gives 277. The רבנן hold it has 71, so one more person is needed (23 + 48 = 71), which gives 278.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult (introduces an answer)

steps.whatToRemember: 277 matches a סנהדרין גדולה of 70 (רבי יהודה); 278 matches one of 71 (רבנן).

phrases.english: It is not difficult: this follows רבי יהודה,
phrases.notes: 'This' means the 277 count. רבי יהודה counts 70 judges in the great court.

phrases.english: that follows the Rabbis.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא – רַבִּי יְהוּדָה, הָא – רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning each source to a different opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two numbers seemed to contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each number follows a different view on the size of the סנהדרין גדולה (70 or 71).

steps.title: Counting the ministers in the desert
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא counts the ministers of thousands, hundreds, fifties, and tens.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: "And place over them ministers of thousands, ministers of hundreds, ministers of fifties, and ministers of tens." Ministers of thousands: 600. Ministers of hundreds: 6,000. Ministers of fifties: 12,000. Ministers of tens: 60,000.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that uses the פסוק about יתרו's advice to count how many judges were appointed in the desert.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There were 600,000 men. Dividing them into groups of 1,000, 100, 50, and 10 gives 600, 6,000, 12,000, and 60,000 ministers. This connects to the earlier discussion, which also linked the size of a court to the ministers in the desert.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
"And place over them ministers of thousands,

phrases.aramaic: שָׂרֵי מֵאוֹת שָׂרֵי חֲמִשִּׁים וְשָׂרֵי עֲשָׂרֹת״.
phrases.english: ministers of hundreds, ministers of fifties, and ministers of tens."
"Ministers of thousands": six hundred,
"Ministers of hundreds": six thousand,
"Ministers of fifties": twelve thousand,
"Ministers of tens": sixty thousand.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: וְשַׂמְתָּ עֲלֵיהֶם שָׂרֵי אֲלָפִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A related ברייתא brought because the earlier discussion linked court size to the ministers in the desert.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ministers were 600 over thousands, 6,000 over hundreds, 12,000 over fifties, and 60,000 over tens.

steps.title: Total judges: 78,600
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא adds everything up: Israel had 78,600 judges.
steps.simpleTranslation: It turns out that the judges of Israel were seventy-eight thousand six hundred.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds up the four groups to reach the total number of judges.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 600 + 6,000 + 12,000 + 60,000 = 78,600. The ministers are called judges here because their job was to judge the people.

keyTerms.meaning: It turns out, the total comes to

steps.whatToRemember: The desert system had 78,600 judges in total: 600 + 6,000 + 12,000 + 60,000.

phrases.english: It turns out the judges of Israel were

phrases.aramaic: שִׁבְעַת רִיבּוֹא וּשְׁמוֹנַת אֲלָפִים וְשֵׁשׁ מֵאוֹת.
phrases.english: seventy thousand, eight thousand, and six hundred.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds up the numbers listed in step 4.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Israel in the desert had 78,600 judges.

steps.title: Hadran: Closing דיני ממונות
steps.stepSummary: The closing line of the first פרק of סנהדרין, פרק דיני ממונות.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, דיני ממונות.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the traditional closing line marking the end of the פרק. The next פרק begins after it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הדרן is not part of the argument. It marks that the first פרק of מסכת סנהדרין, which deals with the makeup of the courts, is finished.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you (said at the end of a פרק)
Monetary cases, the name of the first פרק

phrases.english: We will return to you, Dinei Mamonot.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the whole פרק after its last discussion.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The first פרק of סנהדרין, דיני ממונות, is complete.

steps.title: The כהן גדול in court, testimony, חליצה and יבום
steps.stepSummary: A new פרק opens. The משנה teaches that a כהן גדול judges and can be judged, testifies and can be testified about, and is part of חליצה. He may not do יבום himself, because he may not marry a widow.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A כהן גדול judges others, and others judge him. He testifies, and others testify about him. He does חליצה, and others do חליצה with his wife. Others may do יבום with his wife. But he himself does not do יבום, because he is forbidden to marry a widow.
steps.whatsHappening: A new פרק begins with a משנה about the כהן גדול. It lists where he is treated like a regular person and the one place where he is different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In court and in testimony, the כהן גדול is a normal member of the community: he can judge and be judged. After his death, his brother can do חליצה or יבום with his widow. But he cannot do יבום for his brother's widow, because a כהן גדול may not marry any widow.

keyTerms.meaning: Does חליצה, the ceremony that releases a widow from יבום
Does יבום, marrying a brother's childless widow

steps.confusionAlert: 'His wife' in the חליצה and יבום lines means his widow after he dies. His brother does חליצה or יבום with her, not while the כהן גדול is alive.

phrases.english: MISHNA: A High Priest
judges, and others judge him;
he testifies, and others testify about him;
he performs ḥalitza, and others perform ḥalitza with his wife;
phrases.notes: After he dies, his brother can do חליצה with his widow.

phrases.english: and others may do levirate marriage with his wife.
But he himself does not do levirate marriage,
because he is forbidden to marry a widow.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל דָּן וְדָנִין אוֹתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new פרק right after the closing line of פרק דיני ממונות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כהן גדול judges and is judged, testifies and is testified about, and takes part in חליצה. Others may do יבום with his widow, but he may not do יבום because he may not marry a widow.

steps.title: How the כהן גדול accompanies a relative's funeral
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר teaches that a כהן גדול may not walk behind the coffin. He follows at a distance, staying out of sight of the procession, until the city gate.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a relative of his dies, he does not walk behind the coffin. Rather, when they are out of sight, he comes into view, and when they come into view, he is out of sight. In this way he goes out with them until the entrance of the city gate. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה explains what a כהן גדול does when a close relative dies. According to רבי מאיר, he may accompany the funeral, but only from a distance.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כהן גדול may not become טמא even for a close relative, so he cannot walk right behind the coffin. רבי מאיר still lets him show respect: he trails behind, always one street away and never in view of the procession, all the way to the city gate.

keyTerms.meaning: The bier, the frame used to carry the dead
The entrance of the city gate

phrases.english: If a relative of his dies,
he does not go out after the bier.
Rather, when they are hidden from view, he comes into view;
when they come into view, he is hidden;
and he goes out with them
until the entrance of the city gate.
These are the words of Rabbi Meir.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵת לוֹ מֵת אֵינוֹ יוֹצֵא אַחַר הַמִּטָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of rules about the כהן גדול, now turning to a relative's funeral.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי מאיר, the כהן גדול does not walk behind the coffin. He follows out of sight of the procession until the city gate.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: he does not leave the מקדש at all
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה disagrees with רבי מאיר. He holds that the כהן גדול does not leave the מקדש at all for a funeral, based on a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: He does not go out of the מקדש, because it is said: 'And from the מקדש he shall not go out.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה gives a different opinion from רבי מאיר. He says the כהן גדול stays in the מקדש and does not accompany the funeral at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר let the כהן גדול follow at a distance. רבי יהודה reads the פסוק 'from the מקדש he shall not go out' literally, so the כהן גדול does not leave the מקדש even for that.

keyTerms.meaning: Because it is said; introduces a פסוק as the source

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
He does not go out of the Temple,
because it is said:
"And from the Temple he shall not go out."

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר אֵינוֹ יוֹצֵא מִן הַמִּקְדָּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a disagreeing view to רבי מאיר's ruling about the funeral.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, the כהן גדול does not leave the מקדש at all for a relative's funeral, based on ויקרא 21:12.

steps.title: How the כהן גדול comforts other mourners
steps.stepSummary: When the כהן גדול comforts mourners, people normally pass by one after another. The appointed official stands between him and the people.
steps.simpleTranslation: And when he comforts others: the way of all the people is to pass by one after another, and the appointed official stands in the middle, between him and the people.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves from his own funeral duties to how he comforts other mourners. It describes the order of the line and where the appointed official stands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, comforters pass by the mourners one after another. When the כהן גדול joins, the official appointed under him stands between him and everyone else. This keeps his honor and his place apart from the crowd.

keyTerms.meaning: The appointed official, the deputy under the כהן גדול

phrases.english: And when he comforts others,
the way of all the people is that
they pass by one after another,
and the appointed official stands in the middle, between him and the people.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list of כהן גדול rules, moving from his funeral duties to comforting others.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the כהן גדול comforts mourners, people pass one after another, and the appointed official stands between him and the people.

steps.title: How people comfort the כהן גדול when he is mourning
steps.stepSummary: When people comfort the כהן גדול, they say 'We are your atonement,' and he blesses them. At the mourner's meal, everyone reclines on the ground while he reclines on a bench.
steps.simpleTranslation: And when others comfort him, all the people say to him: 'We are your atonement.' And he says to them: 'May you be blessed from Heaven.' And when they give him the mourner's meal, all the people recline on the ground, and he reclines on the bench.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes the mourning rules by describing what happens when the כהן גדול himself is the mourner. It covers both the words of comfort and the seating at the mourner's meal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even as a mourner, the כהן גדול keeps his special honor. The people express deep devotion to him, and he answers with a blessing. At the meal, the comforters sit on the ground, as if sharing his mourning, while he, the actual mourner, sits on a bench.

keyTerms.meaning: Give the mourner's first meal after the burial

steps.whatToRemember: The opening משנה of this פרק shows the balance of the כהן גדול. He is a regular member of the community in court, but his special holiness changes his rules in יבום, at a funeral, and in mourning.

phrases.english: And when he is comforted by others,
all the people say to him:
We are your atonement.
And he says to them:
May you be blessed from Heaven.
And when they give him the mourner's meal,
all the people recline on the ground,
and he reclines on the bench.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The other side of step 10: there he comforted others, here others comfort him.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When others comfort the כהן גדול, they say 'We are your atonement,' and he blesses them. At the mourner's meal, they recline on the ground and he reclines on a bench.

steps.title: The king does not judge, testify, or take part in חליצה and יבום
steps.stepSummary: The משנה teaches that the king is cut off from the court system, from testimony, and from חליצה and יבום, in both directions.
steps.simpleTranslation: The king does not judge, and nobody judges him. He does not testify, and nobody testifies about him. He does not do חליצה, and nobody does חליצה with his wife. He does not do יבום, and nobody does יבום with his wife.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה turns from the כהן גדול to the king. It lists the things the king is NOT part of.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This list matches the כהן גדול list in Step 7 almost word for word, but every item is negative. The כהן גדול judges and is judged. The king does neither, and the same goes for testimony, חליצה and יבום. Each rule works both ways: the king does not do these things to others, and others do not do them to the king.

keyTerms.meaning: Performs חליצה (the release ceremony instead of יבום)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two lists. The כהן גדול list (Step 7) is mostly 'yes'. The king list here is all 'no'.

phrases.english: The king does not judge,
and others do not judge him,
he does not testify, and others do not testify about him,
he does not perform chalitza, and others do not perform chalitza with his wife,
he does not perform yibum, and others do not perform yibum with his wife.
phrases.notes: 'His wife' means his widow, if the king dies without children.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַמֶּלֶךְ לֹא דָּן, וְלֹא דָּנִין אוֹתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the כהן גדול's laws to the contrasting laws of the king
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The king takes no part in judging, testimony, חליצה or יבום, either as the one doing it or as the one it is done to.

steps.title: רבי יהודה says a king may choose to do חליצה or יבום
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה praises a king who wants to do חליצה or יבום. The חכמים answer that we do not go along with him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: if the king wants to do חליצה or יבום, he is remembered for good. They said to him: we do not listen to him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה argues on the last part of the משנה, and the חכמים reply to him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה says the king may choose to do these מצוות, and it is even praiseworthy. The חכמים say that even if the king wants to, we do not let him. In their view the rule does not depend on his choice.

keyTerms.meaning: We do not listen to him (we don't allow it)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
If he wants to perform chalitza or yibum,
he is remembered for good.
They said to him: We do not listen to him.
phrases.notes: 'Him' is the king: we don't go along with his wish.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אִם רָצָה לַחֲלוֹץ אוֹ לְיַיבֵּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A disagreement with the last clause of the king's list
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה: the king may choose to do חליצה or יבום. חכמים: he is not allowed even if he wants to.

steps.title: Nobody may marry the king's widow
steps.stepSummary: The משנה adds that no one may marry a king's widow.
steps.simpleTranslation: And nobody marries his widow.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds one more rule about the king: his widow may not remarry.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This rule protects the king even after his death. It also connects to the last item in the list: nobody does יבום with his wife, so no one marries her that way either. רבי יהודה will argue on this rule in the next step.

phrases.english: And no one may marry his widow,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another restriction to the king's list
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A king's widow may not remarry.

steps.title: רבי יהודה says another king may marry a king's widow
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה allows a king to marry a former king's widow. He brings proof from דוד, who married the wives of שאול.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: a king may marry another king's widow. We find that דוד married שאול's widow, as the פסוק says: 'I gave you your master's house and your master's wives into your bosom.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה argues on the rule from Step 14 and proves his view from a פסוק about דוד המלך.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה agrees that a regular person may not marry the king's widow. But another king is not a regular person. He proves this from נתן הנביא's words to דוד, which say that ה׳ gave דוד his master שאול's wives.

keyTerms.meaning: For so we find (introduces a proof from an earlier case)
שאול המלך, the king before דוד

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
A king may marry the widow of a king,
for so we found with David
that he married the widow of Saul,
as it is stated:
"And I gave you the house of your master
and the wives of your master into your bosom."

steps.triggerLanguage: נוֹשֵׂא הַמֶּלֶךְ אַלְמְנָתוֹ שֶׁל מֶלֶךְ, שֶׁכֵּן מָצִינוּ בְּדָוִד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with Step 14 and backs it up with a פסוק
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה: a king may marry a previous king's widow.
steps.raayaObject: A king may marry a king's widow
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמואל ב 12:8, where דוד is given שאול's wives
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה is now finished. The כהן גדול judges, is judged and has a part in חליצה. The king has no part in any of these, and his widow may not remarry, though רבי יהודה lets another king marry her.

steps.title: Isn't it obvious that a כהן גדול judges?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking why the משנה needs to say that a כהן גדול may judge.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: 'A כהן גדול judges.' Isn't that obvious?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins. It quotes the first words of the משנה from Step 7 and asks why they need to be said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no reason to think a כהן גדול would be unfit to be a judge. So it seems the משנה is teaching something nobody needed to be told. The גמרא wants to find the new idea in these words.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה

phrases.english: GEMARA:
"A High Priest judges."
phrases.notes: These are the first words of the משנה back in Step 7.

phrases.english: That is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the opening line of the משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה should not teach something obvious, and nobody would think a כהן גדול cannot judge.

steps.title: The real point is that others judge him
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה needed to say the second half, 'others judge him.'
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Others judge him' is what it needed to say.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the new idea is in the second half of the line: a court may judge the כהן גדול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first half, 'he judges', was only said to go along with the second half. The real point is that even a person as important as the כהן גדול can be brought to court. One might have thought his high position protects him.

keyTerms.meaning: It was needed (this is the real point)

phrases.english: "And they judge him"
is what it needed to teach.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 16
steps.terutzResolutionType: Moves the new idea to the second half of the clause
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without the משנה, we might think the כהן גדול is too important to be judged
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is teaching that he can be judged; 'he judges' was only said to go with it

steps.title: Being judged is obvious too, by ריש לקיש's teaching
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: if he judges, he must also be judged, because one must fix himself before fixing others.
steps.simpleTranslation: This too is obvious! If we don't judge him, how could he judge? The פסוק says 'הִתְקוֹשְׁשׁוּ וָקוֹשּׁוּ', and ריש לקיש said: first fix yourself, and then fix others.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer in Step 17. It says the second half is just as obvious as the first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש reads the פסוק as teaching that a person must improve himself before he corrects others. So someone who cannot be judged may not judge others. Since everyone knows the כהן גדול may judge, he must also be subject to judgment, and the משנה has still taught nothing new.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it written? (brings a פסוק as proof)
An אמורא, רבי שמעון בן לקיש

phrases.english: This too is obvious:
if we do not judge him,
how could he judge?
But isn't it written: "Gather yourselves together and gather"?
phrases.notes: צפניה 2:1. ריש לקיש reads these words as 'קשט', to adorn or fix up.

phrases.english: And Reish Lakish said:
Adorn yourself first,
and afterward adorn others.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא נָמֵי פְּשִׁיטָא: אִי לָא דָּיְינִינַן לֵיהּ, אִיהוּ הֵיכִי דָּיֵין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer of Step 17
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that 'others judge him' is the new idea
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Only someone who can be judged may judge others (ריש לקיש). Since the כהן גדול judges, it follows that he is judged, so this is obvious too.
steps.whyThisMatters: ריש לקיש's rule, 'fix yourself first, then fix others', applies far beyond this case. It is a basic rule for anyone who sits in judgment.

steps.title: It was said only to match the king's rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the כהן גדול's rule teaches nothing new. It was said only because the משנה wanted to teach the king's rule next to it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, since the משנה wanted to teach that a king does not judge and is not judged, it also taught that a כהן גדול judges and is judged.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives up on finding something new in the כהן גדול line. It explains that the line is there for the sake of the king's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new teaching is really about the king. The כהן גדול's rule is set beside it to show the contrast and keep the משנה balanced. So the 'obvious' line is there for style, not because it adds a new law.

keyTerms.meaning: Since / because (it was going to say something else)

phrases.english: Rather, since it wants to teach

phrases.aramaic: מֶלֶךְ לֹא דָּן וְלֹא דָּנִין אוֹתוֹ,
phrases.english: "A king does not judge and others do not judge him,"
it also taught
"A High Priest judges and is judged."

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, אַיְּידֵי דְּקָא בָּעֵי לְמִיתְנֵי מֶלֶךְ לֹא דָּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the challenge of Step 18 and explains the line in a new way
steps.terutzResolutionType: Parallel structure: the obvious line is there only to stand beside the king's rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every line in the משנה must teach a new law
steps.terutzMaskana: The כהן גדול's line is there for contrast with the king's rule

steps.title: Second answer: the כהן גדול is treated like an ordinary person
steps.stepSummary: Another answer: the משנה is teaching what a ברייתא says, that a כהן גדול is treated like an ordinary person in all his laws.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or you can say: this teaches us what the ברייתא says. A כהן גדול who killed someone on purpose is killed. If he killed by accident, he goes into exile. He can break a positive מצוה or a prohibition, and he is like an ordinary person in all his matters.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a second answer. It says the משנה does teach something real and supports this with a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Others judge him' means the כהן גדול gets no special treatment. If he murders on purpose, he gets the death penalty. If he kills by accident, he goes to an עיר מקלט. He is punished for his sins like anyone else. His high position does not protect him from the law.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you want, say (introduces another answer)
This is what it teaches us
Goes into exile (to an עיר מקלט)

steps.whatToRemember: There are two answers for why the משנה says a כהן גדול judges and is judged. 1) It was said only to stand beside the king's rule. 2) It teaches that the כהן גדול is like an ordinary person before the law.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
this teaches us what was taught in a baraita:
A High Priest who killed a person,
if on purpose, he is killed;
if by accident, he goes into exile;

phrases.aramaic: וְעוֹבֵר עַל עֲשֵׂה וְעַל לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה,
phrases.english: and he can transgress a positive מצוה and a prohibition,
phrases.notes: He means the כהן גדול is held responsible for breaking מצוות, just like anyone else.

phrases.english: and he is like an ordinary person in all his matters.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי בָּעֵית אֵימָא, הָא קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן כִּדְתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to the challenge of Steps 16 and 18, different from Step 19
steps.terutzResolutionType: Finds a real new teaching in the line by linking it to a ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We might think the כהן גדול's high position exempts him from regular punishments
steps.terutzMaskana: The כהן גדול is fully subject to the law, like an ordinary person
steps.whyThisMatters: It sets a basic rule: even the highest religious leader is not above the law.

steps.title: Why say he is killed if he killed on purpose?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא's first clause: of course a כהן גדול who murders on purpose is put to death.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he killed on purpose, he is put to death. That is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא looks at the first part of the ברייתא, that a כהן גדול who kills on purpose is put to death, and asks why this needed to be said at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lists rules for a כהן גדול who kills. Nobody would think a murderer escapes punishment just because he is the כהן גדול. So the גמרא asks what the clause adds.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious, so why say it?

phrases.english: If on purpose, he is put to death: that is obvious!
phrases.notes: This quotes the ברייתא from the last step: a כהן גדול who kills on purpose is put to death.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Examines the wording of the ברייתא brought in step 20
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A clause that states something obvious seems to teach nothing new

steps.title: The point is the 'by accident' clause
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the 'on purpose' clause is only there as a lead-in. The real teaching is that a כהן גדול who kills by accident goes into exile.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was the part 'if by accident, he is exiled' that the ברייתא needed to say.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא really needed the second part: a כהן גדול who kills by accident is sent to an עיר מקלט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'on purpose' clause is not the real teaching. It was said only to set up the 'by accident' clause, and that clause is what the ברייתא wanted to teach. This follows the same pattern as step 17.

keyTerms.meaning: Goes into exile to an עיר מקלט
He needed it, meaning that is the part the text needed to say

phrases.english: It needed the part 'if by accident, he is exiled.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 21
steps.terutzResolutionType: The obvious clause was said for the sake of the next, needed clause
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The 'on purpose' clause seemed to be pointless
steps.terutzMaskana: The new teaching is in the 'by accident, he is exiled' clause

steps.title: Isn't the exile rule obvious too?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: it is also obvious that a כהן גדול who kills by accident goes into exile, just like anyone else.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is also obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer it just gave. The 'by accident' clause seems just as obvious as the first one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Anyone who kills by accident goes to an עיר מקלט. Why would a כהן גדול be different? So the second clause also seems to add nothing.

phrases.english: This too is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 22
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Exile for accidental killing applies to everyone, so saying it for a כהן גדול seems unnecessary

steps.title: We might have thought a כהן גדול is not exiled
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the clause was needed. Since the פסוק ties the end of exile to the death of the כהן גדול, we might think only someone who can eventually go home is exiled. A כהן גדול who killed has no such way back. The גמרא begins to bring a משנה to show this.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was needed. You might have thought this: since it is written, 'And he shall live in it until the death of the כהן גדול,' anyone who has a fix by returning home is exiled, and anyone who has no fix by returning home is not exiled. As we learned in a משנה:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the 'by accident' clause is not obvious after all. It then starts quoting a משנה to back up its reasoning, and that משנה comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה says the accidental killer goes home when the כהן גדול dies. So exile seems built around having a way to go home in the end. A כהן גדול who killed has no such way out, so we might have said he is not exiled at all. The ברייתא teaches that he is exiled anyway.

keyTerms.meaning: It would have entered your mind to say, meaning you might have thought
A fix, a way to set things right
By returning home from the עיר מקלט
As we learned in a משנה

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא's 'by accident, he is exiled' clause teaches something new. Even though a כהן גדול who killed has no way back home through a כהן גדול's death, he is still sent to an עיר מקלט.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two כהנים גדולים. The פסוק is about the death of the כהן גדול in office, which frees the killer. Here the killer himself is the כהן גדול, so the משנה about to be quoted shows he has no way back.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that being sent to an עיר מקלט does not depend on having a way to go home later. Exile applies even when there is no release.

phrases.english: It was needed, because you might have thought:
Since it is written
'And he shall live in it until the death of the High Priest,'

phrases.aramaic: אֵימָא: כֹּל דְּאִית לֵיהּ תַּקַּנְתָּא בַּחֲזָרָה – לִיגְלֵי,
phrases.english: say: whoever has a fix by returning home should be exiled,

phrases.aramaic: דְּלֵית לֵיהּ תַּקַּנְתָּא בַּחֲזָרָה – לָא לִיגְלֵי,
phrases.english: but one who has no fix by returning home should not be exiled,
as we learned in a Mishnah:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 23 and sets up a supporting משנה
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows a reasonable mistaken assumption that the clause rules out
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since exile ends with the כהן גדול's death, someone with no way to return, like a כהן גדול who killed, would not be exiled
steps.terutzMaskana: A כהן גדול who kills by accident is exiled even though he has no way to return
